stories.title: Assessment of the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of oral and maxillofacial surgeons in Türkiye regarding oral potentially malignant disorders and oral cancer
stories.description: Early detection of oral cancer improves survival, and oral and maxillofacial surgeons (OMFSs) play a central role in diagnosing and managing oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) and oral cancer. This national cross-sectional online survey evaluated the knowledge, attitudes and clinical practices of OMFSs in Türkiye. Between March and April 2026, 130 OMFSs (84 specialists, 46 residents) completed a 21-item expert-reviewed questionnaire. Self-reported routine oral examination for signs of oral cancer was reported by 60.8% of participants, but only 35.4% routinely examined cervical lymph nodes. Most participants correctly identified smoking as a risk factor (95.4%) and the earliest clinical sign of oral cancer (88.5%); fewer correctly identified the characteristics of suspicious lymph nodes (36.2%) and the typical site of HPV-associated cancers (46.9%). In exploratory analyses, university-based OMFSs more often reported routine oral examination, lymph node examination and documentation of suspicious lesions. Although 67.7% had made a preliminary diagnosis of oral cancer, only 45.4% felt competent to diagnose OPMDs and oral cancer. Nearly all (99.2%) requested further education, and 59.2% disagreed that residency training on oral cancer was adequate. These findings suggest a need to strengthen residency and continuing education on oral cancer examination and early diagnosis.
